sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
In Racine County the town, village or city sends your bill and takes the first payment. The Racine County Treasurer collects what comes after. Bills are prepared and mailed in December. Every municipality except the City of Racine allows two installments, due January 31 and July 31, and the first one goes to the local treasurer.

The County Treasurer's office is on the 1st floor, north end, of the Racine County Courthouse at 730 Wisconsin Avenue. Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday. Call (262) 636-3239 or write to rctreasurer@racinecounty.gov. The county keeps a page of municipal contacts for the Towns of Burlington, Dover, Norway and Waterford, the Villages of Caledonia, Elmwood Park, Mount Pleasant, North Bay, Raymond, Rochester, Sturtevant, Union Grove, Waterford, Wind Point and Yorkville, and the Cities of Burlington and Racine.

sections.h2: Racine County for a home seller
sections.html: The county runs along Lake Michigan in southeastern Wisconsin, with Milwaukee County to the north and Kenosha County to the south. The 2025 population estimate is 198,919, and 67.7 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. A lakeshore city, suburban villages and farm towns share one county, so two houses a few miles apart can have different installment dates and different assessors. Find out which municipality your parcel is in before you quote any date to a buyer.

Four offices cover most of a sale: the municipal assessor, the local or county treasurer, the Register of Deeds and the Board of Review clerk. These are the county-level contacts.

You can pay the County Treasurer at the counter, in the drop box, by mail or online. The counter takes cash, checks and money orders. The drop box on the east side of the courthouse, facing Wisconsin Avenue, does not take cash. Mail goes to Racine County Treasurer, 730 Wisconsin Ave, Racine, WI 53403-1274.

  • Credit card or electronic check: call (800) 272-9829 or pay at OfficialPayments.com with jurisdiction code 5835. Third-party fees apply.
  • Online lookup: the Ascent Land Records site shows the tax record. You need the 15-digit parcel ID or tax key number to pay.
  • Alerts: owners can sign up for text and email notices on their tax parcels.

The treasurer's pages also carry brochures on paying real estate taxes, taxpayer help, tax foreclosure and a glossary of tax terms, plus a short guide to finding your payment history.

When any installment is late or comes up short, everything still owed becomes due at once. Interest of 1 percent per month plus a 0.5 percent monthly penalty, 1.5 percent in all, starts on February 1 under Wis. Stat. s. 74.47. The treasurer has no power to waive it.

State law gives a small cushion. Under s. 74.11(7) the first installment is not delinquent until five working days after January 31 pass without payment. In a year when January 31 lands on a weekend, that cushion runs into the first week of February. Even so, the county treats interest as running from February 1 once a payment is missed, so pay by January 31 when you can.

If you already owe back taxes, the County Treasurer encourages a regular payment plan and accepts monthly payments toward delinquent bills. Ask for a payoff figure before you pick a closing date.

Racine County takes properties through tax foreclosure and then sells them at public sales run by the County Treasurer. There are three kinds: sealed bid, subsequent sealed bid and over-the-counter. You can join a buyers' email list for sale notices, and the Sheriff's Sale site covers sheriff's sales separately.

The treasurer also publishes a Tax Foreclosure FAQ brochure. An owner with several unpaid years who wants to sell does best to close before foreclosure starts. Begin by asking the treasurer which years are open and what the full payoff is.

Assessment disputes go to the municipal Board of Review, never the County Treasurer. Each town, village and city runs its own board. The clerk must post notice at least 15 days before the first session, or 30 days in a revaluation year. Ask your clerk or assessor each spring when open book and the board meet.

  • Tell the board clerk, in writing or by phone, at least 48 hours before the first meeting, unless you show good cause during the first two hours of that meeting.
  • File a written objection with the clerk in those first two hours.
  • Object to land and buildings together. Under s. 70.47(7)(a) you cannot object to just one of them.
  • Expect to testify under oath. The owner and any witnesses speak first.

sections.h2: Tax credits that lower a bill
sections.html:
Two credits come up most often. The lottery and gaming credit reduces the tax on a qualified home, and owners apply for it or remove it through the Department of Revenue's online portal. Late claims must go through that portal by October 1.

The homestead credit is separate. You claim it on your Wisconsin income tax return, and it is meant to ease property tax and rent costs for people with lower incomes. The county links to a Department of Revenue fact sheet for checking eligibility, and it also links a veteran's credit page.

sections.h2: Recording a deed at the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is at 730 Wisconsin Avenue and takes documents by drop-off, mail or e-filing. If you do not e-file, use a title company or an electronic recording service provider. Public computers for record searches are open from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, first come, first served, and staff cannot do the search for you.

State rules set the cost. Recording a document is $30 under s. 59.43(2)(ag). The real estate transfer fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value under s. 77.22. Transfers by will or survivorship are exempt, as are certain family transfers for nominal consideration.

Work through it in this order.

  1. Pull the parcel record and note which years are open.
  2. Call the treasurer who is collecting your installments and ask for the full payoff, with interest.
  3. Give that figure to the title company so it comes out of the sale proceeds.
  4. Record the deed and file the transfer return.

Where you sell matters. A house in the City of Racine runs on four installments, while one in Mount Pleasant or Caledonia runs on two. After July 31, every payment, City of Racine parcels included, goes to the County Treasurer.

The tax payoff, the deed and the transfer return apply to every sale, whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan. Check each figure against the county's tax record before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Racine County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay your local municipality for the first installment. Pay the Racine County Treasurer at 730 Wisconsin Avenue for second installments and delinquent taxes. The City of Racine collects its own four installments through July 31.

faqs.q: What is the Racine County treasurer's phone number?
faqs.a: Call (262) 636-3239. The office is in the courthouse at 730 Wisconsin Avenue and is open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: What interest do late taxes carry in Racine County?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes carry 1 percent interest and a 0.5 percent penalty per month, 1.5 percent in total, under Wis. Stat. s. 74.47. The county cannot forgive it.

faqs.q: Can I pay Racine County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Call (800) 272-9829 or use OfficialPayments.com with jurisdiction code 5835. Third-party fees apply, and the drop box does not accept cash.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Racine County?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 under Wis. Stat. s. 59.43(2)(ag). The transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value under s. 77.22 unless an exemption applies. Call the Register of Deeds at (262) 636-3208 to confirm.
